claims.text: The initial component is based on the high-entropy boride (TiZrHfTaNb)B2.
High-temperature sintering can produce a chemically homogeneous (TiZrHfTaNb)B2 matrix.
Laser surface alloying with silicon will create a Si-enriched superficial layer on the high-entropy boride.
Optimization of the laser parameters and silicon feed will make the Si-enriched layer continuous and uniform.
A laser power density of approximately 1 MW/cm² with a calibrated scan rate can produce an approximately 20 μm melt depth.
Exposure to molten aluminum at approximately 670°C for 10–60 minutes simulates typical hot-dip aluminum-plating conditions.
Laser alloying with silicon will locally convert the boride matrix into a (Ti,Si)B2 or Si–B-rich intermetallic phase.
The proposed Si-containing phase will act as a barrier to molten aluminum.
Silicon incorporation can facilitate formation of a continuous passivating protective layer.
The Si-enriched layer will decrease the wettability of the surface by molten aluminum.
The Si-enriched layer will decrease chemical reactivity between the boride and molten aluminum.
The Si-enriched layer will reduce interdiffusion between the boride substrate and molten aluminum.
Silicon-assisted protective-layer formation will significantly reduce molten-aluminum corrosion relative to an untreated surface.
The treatment may reduce weight loss by roughly 50% relative to untreated specimens.
Laser-alloyed specimens will retain better surface-microstructure integrity after molten-aluminum exposure.
Improved corrosion resistance will remain effective only when the laser process produces a uniform, continuous Si-enriched layer.
A non-uniform or discontinuous layer caused by suboptimal laser parameters or silicon feed will compromise the corrosion-resistance benefit.

contradictions.description: The boundary states that the benefit is expected only when a continuous layer is successfully produced, but the falsification rule treats failure to produce such a layer as falsification of the hypothesis rather than as failure to instantiate the stipulated intervention.
